The analytic chamber containment and metric-ball cutoff justify the finite enumeration; no floating-point or partial enumeration is presented as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full material was read for the 2026 primary paper and the two closest published mathematical records. They supply an outer 41-vertex chamber, covering radius, 576 deepest-hole incidences, 192 deepest Delaunay simplices and metric-ray optimization. They do not state, compute or imply the actual 74-facet/864-vertex simple cell, complete face vector, 288 shallower Voronoi vertices, or 96 additional small Delaunay simplices without the new full incidence calculation. Targeted published-finding corpus and external term/number/dual-formulation searches found no equivalent. This is best-knowledge same-model originality, not independent priority certification.
residual_risks: The companion note by Mathieu Dutour Sikirić, titled Non-lattice periodic point sets for the packing-covering problem: ties, structure and search, cited by the primary paper, could not be inspected in full text. It might include a facet or Delone census.
Unindexed computational classifications of the same five-dimensional periodic set may exist.
Independent scholarly priority verification has not been performed.

value.rationale: A complete f-vector and exact two-shell Delone/Delaunay tiling of the exceptional 2026 nonlattice packing is a naturally motivated structural classification. It resolves the previously unspecified remaining one-fifth of the Delaunay tessellation into exactly 96 determinant-1/2 simplices, and determines 74 facet orbits, 864 simple vertices and all face counts. This is an unknown exact natural invariant supporting subsequent geometry and stability work, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
